title: Alabama theater where Black audiences were afraid to applaud
summary: In an Alabama white theater the manager set aside one day for Black patrons, who packed the house and tapped their feet but dared not applaud.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah. Anyway, we worked everywhere. We went down one -- we had to laugh at that -- we was down in, I think it was Alabama somewhere and played in this theater and it was strictly white, you know. So they decided, the manager decided to give one night to the Negroes. So the night those Negroes -- I mean, the day, in fact, the whole day it was packed and jammed for every show. But the funny part about it, we'd play a number or whatever you could see their feet patting on the floor. No applause. They wouldn't -- they were afraid to applaud.

Who knows? And when the last show, when we'd be off going to the train and we could hear them say, 'Oh, what a band. Jesus, what a band,' and nobody -- no applause or nothing. But they didn't -- they were stupid enough to know that if they would applaud, they would get more music, you know. But no, no applause. But they were just afraid.
